Great omakase experience with a humble and friendly chef
Sep 2018 • Couples
Disclaimer: I am no sushi expert, although well traversed in the world of low-end/mid-end sushi, omakase sushi is totally different ball game in which I have less experience with. After comparing the sushi omakases in HCMC this seemed like a place worth trying.

We called in on a Monday at 6pm and booked a table for 7 pm. The place has about 6-8 seats in front of the sushibar, but you're also able to sit upstairs or downstairs, although I don't think the experience would be the same. Chef Hung is young, but has been in the game for approximately 10 years. He makes great effort in giving you high quality sushi that's worthy of being called authentic. We could choose between 500k, 700k or 900k set menu where the main difference is the size. Seemed like there was a decent selection of of Sake as well. We were served sashimi (some of which had a little Vietnamese inspired twist), nigiri (in which some of them were lightly flambéed), as well as a fish/miso soup and a braised mackerel dish. The fish was fresh and the other cooked dishes gave the whole meal an added touch. 

I think Tripadvisor and many other reviewing sites has become inflated with their scores, but I wholeheartedly give top score and my unreserved recommendations for this place and for chef Hung. Reasonably priced place with an aspiring, extremely down to earth and humble Vietnamese chef who's traditionally trained in the art. I wish him the best of luck in the future, and will definitely return next time I'm in HCMC.

Decent omakase
Apr 2018 • Friends
We found this place from a friend’s post and was intrigued by the concept. I went there twice to make sure this review is correct. The first time, I tried their 500k vnd set and the second time the 1 mil vnd menu. 

For the price, you are getting some decent sushi/ sashimi/ cooked foods and soup. I’m a bit of a sushi snob and have dined all over the world. While the food is not world class, it’s one of the best in Saigon. It’s obvious the chef has been trained by a traditional Japanese sushi chef. However, he has yet to perfect his craft. I was served a piece of red snapper sushi with two half slices. While I understand the costs involved, that nigiri should have never been served. The toppings, while unique to Saigon, are just soy sauce mixed with bonito flakes and it’s placed on random items.

They did have a decent sake selection albeit at an inflated price and I had wished it was served much colder. Chilled glasses would have been better. 

I was so encouraged to see a Vietnamese chef trying to perfect the art of sushi and I wish the chef best of luck.

An authentic sushi experience outside Japan
May 2018 • Couples
We booked late so the sushi counter was full, but they put us at the tempura counter, which was on the floor above. I was pleasantly surprised from the start. Everything we had was at the good Japanese sushi restaurant standard. Since the chef wasn't in front of us, if I wasn't told the fact that he was a young Vietnamese, I would have imagined a Japanese chef with at least a decade of experience but still kind of edgy to try some new styles too. Though it was a busy Friday night, everything went smoothly, and we only saw calm, genuine smiles there. The price is incredibly reasonable for the quality they provide. After the first visit to the restaurant, I have been regularly visiting the bar downstairs. Thank you for always welcoming me with a big smile :) See you again very soon!

Amazing Experience and Best sushi in HCM
Aug 2017 • Couples
It is a tiny 9 seat sushi bar above a Cowboy type bar. It is down one of the alleys on Le Thanh Ton. But the search is well worth it!!! Chef Hung and manager Eeri do an amazing job both with presentation and taste. From the salmon, tamago and tuna, everything was on point. It was amazing to see the personal care and touch the chef put on each piece. My personal favorite was the new tastes from the lightly seared pieces of fish. Note they only have roughly one seating per night, and due to small size, you have to make a reservation a week in advance.
